sources.name: NASA 3D Resources: Z2 Spacesuit 3D model (the crew figures in the walk, the walk-through and the replay)
sources.provider: NASA / Langley Research Center, Advanced Concepts Lab (model); NASA Science (3D Resources hub)

access.notes: glTF binary, 16,933,148 bytes, sha256 4199762c27f8e730030a7bf9f1a453c203457e84c33b36247c0237a74f9a0c2a, downloaded 2026-11-15 00:59 UTC into data/raw/nasa3d/ (git-ignored). 30,904 triangles, about 1.93 m tall, no skeleton and no animation.

The 3D Resources hub: 'All of these assets are free to download and use', with NASA's Brand & Usage and Images and Media Usage Guidelines. The GitHub mirror (github.com/nasa/NASA-3D-Resources) says the assets are 'free and without copyright'.

sources.license: NASA 3D Resources: free to download and use (NASA media usage guidelines); no endorsement by NASA implied
sources.credit: Z2 Spacesuit 3D model: NASA/LaRC/Advanced Concepts Lab, via NASA 3D Resources (cleaned copy)

verified.notes: The model page and the file answered 200 on 2026-11-15. The file was opened: one mesh 'Z2' (Draco-compressed), one material 'Baked', three pictures (colour, bump, specular), each as WebP plus a JPEG copy. The app ships a copy made by pipeline/baramger_pipeline/suit_model.py: app/public/models/z2-spacesuit.glb, 939,796 bytes, sha256 40ce0b338cbe1b373b4044e439c111cea85b7d677e79eccae034b5d3ebb298fd. Same mesh and material; without the JPEG copies; without the bump picture (strength 0 in NASA's file, but drawn by CesiumJS); and with the grime painted on the white fabric taken off the colour picture (seams, stripes, black parts, flag and patches kept), at the user's request (2026-11-15).

caveats: Extra source under D2. C1: a NASA model from NASA Langley, served by NASA (assets.science.nasa.gov); no China link. C2: NASA says the 3D Resources are free to download and use. C3: opened and checked against its page (source, file size, date). C4: an official NASA product with a known date (page 15 Apr 2025, file 27 Feb 2025) and resolution (30,904 triangles, 4096-px pictures); how closely it matches the real Z2 suit is not documented. C5: a model of a real NASA prototype suit (made for walking on planets), not AI-made. It is a picture of the crew, not map data: nothing is measured or computed from it.
The figures are drawn at the model's own size (about 1.93 m). From the tablet's top view (camera about 380 m up) they are only a few pixels tall, so the round crew marker stays there.
The model cannot move its legs (no skeleton): the figures glide along the route and turn to face the way they go.

The suit carries small NASA and US flag patches, as the real one does. NASA's brand guidelines say the NASA insignia must not suggest that NASA endorses a product; at the size the app draws them they are a few pixels.
The app's copy changes NASA's colour picture (grime taken off) and leaves two of its pictures out; the mesh is NASA's.

layers.title: Viking colour mosaic (global, natural colour)
layers.attribution: NASA Ames and USGS Astrogeology Science Center (Viking Orbiter colourised mosaic, MDIM 2.1), via Mars Trek
caveats: Cached tiles: 170 of 170 requested

Natural colour, approximate: a colourised mosaic. NASA Ames blended the Viking orbiters' colour mosaic (photos from 1976-1980) over the grey MDIM 2.1 mosaic. USGS published the result in 2009. Producer's record: https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/search/map/mars_viking_colorized_global_mosaic_232m
Level 7 is the finest level Mars Trek serves (about 326 m per pixel; the mosaic itself is 232 m). It is cached around Jezero, and level 3 for the rest of the planet. Far-away context only.
The mosaic shows joins between Viking photos in places (for example about 250 km north of Jezero). They are in the source data.

layers.title: CTX photo mosaic, Jezero crater and around it (preliminary)
caveats: Cached tiles: 110 of 110 requested

Mars Trek calls this mosaic preliminary. It lies about 80 m south of the controlled CTX mosaic (measured on three tiles) and shows seams between image strips: far-away context only, not for positions.
Cached to level 10 (about 40 m per pixel) for the crater and about 14 km around it. A very wide or a tall window shows more than that: the planet map is at its edges then.
The mosaic has one gap of about 3 km2 just south-west of the crater rim (near 77.38 E, 17.98 N). The planet map shows through there. The gap is in the source data.

layers.title: CTX photo mosaic, west side of Jezero crater (controlled)
caveats: Cached tiles: 89 of 89 requested

Cached to level 11 (about 20 m per pixel) for the whole controlled mosaic. It covers the western 40% of Jezero crater (the delta and both walk zones); the 6 m detail is cached only around the walk zone.

layers.title: Weather measured here (Perseverance MEDA)

values.meaning: air and ground temperature, pressure; sunrise and sunset

layers.process: Daily min/max and hourly medians over sols 653-659. Sunrise/sunset computed with Mars24 equations (checked: within 0.5 min of the rover's feed; equation of time within 0.08 min of MEDA's clocks).
caveats: Reference conditions from Dec 2022, when Perseverance was here; not today's weather.

values.meaning: solar flares (7 days) and >=10 MeV proton level (3 days)

caveats: GOES satellites near Earth (1 AU). Mars is about 1.5 AU from the Sun and often on another side, so storms seen here may or may not reach Mars.

site.name: Three Forks (zone Z1)
site.description: The Three Forks sample depot at the foot of the old river delta, where Perseverance left 10 sample tubes in Dec 2022 - Jan 2023.

objectives.title: Collect the sample tubes at Three Forks
objectives.question: Can the crew find the ten sample tubes Perseverance left here, check them and bring them back?
objectives.whyHumans: People can spot a tube under dust, check it closely, and carry several at once.

objectives.title: Read the rocks at the foot of the delta
objectives.question: What do the rocks around the depot say about the old river delta?
objectives.whyHumans: Walking between the spots lets a geologist compare rocks and pick extra samples.

Maximum slope allowed on foot (steeper = no-go)
Walking speed on flat ground in a suit, carrying the standard kit (A17)
assumptions.reference: Speed on slopes scaled with Tobler's hiking function. Carried load changes the time (A15-A21)

assumptions.statement: Walk (EVA) length
Time kept in reserve for the walk back
Habitat position chosen by the planner: flat ground with the best radio view of the walk; not a real landing site
Habitat radio antenna height above ground
Suit radio antenna height above ground
Longest time allowed without radio contact to the habitat
Start the walk at least this long after sunrise
Be back at least this long before sunset
Postpone the walk if the 10 MeV proton level reaches this (NOAA S1 storm level, measured near Earth)
Take extra care for this long after an X-class solar flare
Each depot stop is where the rover parked during depot building (sols 652-692, site 32); the tube dropped then lies within a few metres
assumptions.reference: NASA depot map PIA25682 (image); rover positions from S1

assumptions.statement: Astronaut body mass (load model)
assumptions.reference: NASA JSC, Mars Spacesuit Mass Requirements, ICES-2026-127 (2026), NTRS 20260005410: average male crew member 180 lbm (82 kg). A planning value, not a measurement

assumptions.statement: Mass of a Mars spacesuit with its life support
assumptions.reference: NASA JSC ICES-2026-127 (2026): estimated maximum Mars suit mass 229 lbm (104 kg); today's Artemis xEMU is 376 lbm (170 kg). An estimate, not a measured suit

assumptions.statement: Standard kit each astronaut carries from the start (tools, camera, sample bags); walking speed A3 applies with this kit
assumptions.reference: Starting value chosen for Baramger, below the 50 lbm (22.7 kg) of tools and samples in NASA's Mars suit sizing (ICES-2026-127)

assumptions.statement: Mass of one Mars 2020 sample tube with its sample
assumptions.reference: JPL (21 Dec 2020): each empty tube weighs less than 57 g; about 20 g of sample added (estimate). https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/a-martian-roundtrip-nasas-perseverance-rover-sample-tubes/

assumptions.statement: Mass of one rock sample taken by the crew
assumptions.reference: Starting value for a field-geology hand sample. For scale: Apollo returned 382 kg in 2,196 samples, about 0.17 kg each (NASA)

assumptions.statement: Carried load per astronaut above which to take care
assumptions.reference: NASA JSC ICES-2026-127 (2026): 50 lbm (22.7 kg) of tools and samples per astronaut assumed in Mars suit sizing

assumptions.statement: Most load one astronaut may carry; more is too heavy and the plan cannot be approved
assumptions.reference: Starting value chosen for Baramger; to verify with suited load tests (NASA plans ARGOS tests with varied mass)

assumptions.statement: Height of the person drawn in the map's scale card (a person in a suit)
assumptions.reference: A round value, the same as the suit antenna height (A8). A drawing for scale, not a measurement
